The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's own solution, written from the README and topic pages, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. 158 one-change variants of that solution, plus a half-solved project, were each run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. They include every shape named in the loop-4 reconciliation's closed lists for ops-sme-003 (S1-S14), 008 (a1-a3 and the loop-2 lists), 010 (c1-c7, b1-b3), the guard list g1-g7/f1-f8 and the heredoc list H1-H9. The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. Wrong prerequisite claim that breaks setup. README line 45, lab.json line 60 ("3.10 or later") and tests/setup_python.mjs line 23 (minor >= 10) all accept Python 3.10, but two of the pinned test packages require 3.11: PyPI lists requires_python ">=3.11" for starlette 1.10.0 and for annotated-doc 0.0.7, and the installed METADATA agrees. Reproduced with the lab's own pip: pip install --dry-run --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.10 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 -r tests/requirements.txt stops with "No matching distribution found for annotated-doc==0.0.7" ("0.0.7 Requires-Python >=3.11"); the same command resolves all 14 pins for 3.11, 3.14 and 3.15 on Linux, macOS arm64 and win_amd64. So a learner whose python3 is 3.10 (the default python3 of Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, or a py -3 that selects 3.10) passes the version check and gets a .venv, and then pip fails. A 3.10 interpreter was not available here, so the downstream state was simulated: tests/service.test.mjs run with LAB_PYTHON pointing at a venv that has no packages (the state a failed pip leaves) reports, for each of tests 24-26, "the service check could not run (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'): if this names a missing module, run the setup command once, from the tests folder: npm run setup". From reading setup_python.mjs line 29 (not from a 3.10 run): following that advice, or the troubleshooting line (install a newer Python, run npm run setup again), does not recover. Venv creation is skipped whenever .venv/bin/python (or Scripts\python.exe) already exists, so pip runs again inside the stale 3.10 venv and fails the same way until the learner deletes .venv by hand.
findings.recommendation: Raise the floor to Python 3.11 in README line 45, lab.json prerequisites and setup_python.mjs (minor >= 11), and make the setup message name 3.11. In setup_python.mjs, check the existing venv's own version and recreate .venv when it is below the floor (or when pip fails), and say in Troubleshooting to delete .venv if setup fails after a Python upgrade. Alternatively, pin starlette and annotated-doc versions that still support 3.10, then rerun the dry-run resolution for 3.10.

The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. The service harness hides the learner's own exception. TestClient is built with raise_server_exceptions=False (line 71), and the scenario records only the status and the stand-in's calls, so an exception raised before the HTTPX request is sent becomes "500 (an exception escaped unhandled)" with no type or text. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's own solution, written from the README and topic pages, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. 158 one-change variants of that solution, plus a half-solved project, were each run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. They include every shape named in the loop-4 reconciliation's closed lists for ops-sme-003 (S1-S14), 008 (a1-a3 and the loop-2 lists), 010 (c1-c7, b1-b3), the guard list g1-g7/f1-f8 and the heredoc list H1-H9. The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. A correct solution fails tests 24-26 on a machine that exports a SOCKS proxy. serviceRun passes the whole host environment to Python (line 35: env: { ...process.env, ... }). HTTPX honours proxy variables by default (trust_env), so with ALL_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:1 in the environment, tests/service.test.mjs run alone against the critic's 26/26 solution gives 0/3 (tests 24-26 all fail). Each failure carries the same misleading no-call messages as ops-sme-r5-03. With HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY set to http://127.0.0.1:1 instead, the same run gives 3/3. The http:// case passes because HTTPX's proxy transport is also an HTTPTransport, so the patch covers it. Shell-wide SOCKS settings (ALL_PROXY from VPN or proxy tools) are a plausible minority learner setup, and nothing in the README or Troubleshooting hints at it. The stand-in design also means no proxy is ever needed here.
findings.recommendation: Run service_behavior.py with the proxy variables removed (ALL_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY and their lowercase forms), or set NO_PROXY=* for that child, the way runStep already scrubs the bash environment. Together with ops-sme-r5-03, surface any exception raised before the call.

The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. The step runner does not model the runner's own environment, so correct login steps that read it are falsely rejected with misleading messages. The env built at lines 143-152 sets only PATH, HOME, DOCKER_CONFIG, LANG, GITHUB_ACTIONS and the workflow's env values. GitHub's default variables (GITHUB_EVENT_NAME, GITHUB_REF and others) and the per-step file-command paths (GITHUB_ENV, GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, GITHUB_PATH) are absent, and fill() turns any non-secrets/env expression into the placeholder "lab-expression-not-evaluated". The opposite polarity (GITHUB_EVENT_NAME != pull_request) passes only because the variable is empty. Separately, a login step that first appends a line to "$GITHUB_ENV" stops with ": No such file or directory" under bash -e and fails test 6, although it is valid on a runner. GitHub documents GITHUB_EVENT_NAME as "The name of the event that triggered the workflow." and GITHUB_ENV as "The path on the runner to the file that sets variables from workflow commands." (variables reference, retrieved 2026-11-19T05:38:21Z).
findings.recommendation: Give each step run a modelled push-to-main context: GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push, GITHUB_REF=refs/heads/main, GITHUB_REF_NAME=main, and empty temporary files for GITHUB_ENV, GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and GITHUB_PATH inside the step's temp folder. Fill the github.event_name, github.ref and github.ref_name expressions with the same values (lab.mjs already models them in RUNS). The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. Regression of a binding must-fail shape. The loop-4 reconciliation's closed list for ops-sme-003 names (S7) "xxd given V by here-string" as a shape that must fail test 7, and the loop-2 q2 list bound under ops-sme-r1-02 and ops-sme-r1-07 names "a here-string into base64 or xxd". findings.recommendation: In leaks(), also test a normalised copy of the log: remove all whitespace and xxd/od offset columns (for example by matching every [0-9a-f] run and joining them), then look for the hex form. Also join the ASCII column of each dump line, or simply compare against the log with all whitespace and line breaks removed for the raw form. Re-run S1-S14 afterwards.

evidence.section: Masking a value in a log

findings.recommendation: Exempt only lines that start with "::add-mask::" (after optional leading whitespace), and keep searching the rest of each line otherwise.

findings.recommendation: Either re-rule g7 and the ops-sme-010 kept-passing form as superseded by README rule 1 (the critic's preference, since the lab asks for 401), or accept 422 in test 25 when the stand-in received no request. Either way, record the ruling, and decide whether the f1-f3/f7 wording clause survives the behavioural grader.

The comment at lines 125-126 and the dispatch at line 127 match GitHub's shell table, retrieved 2026-11-19T05:17:59Z: unspecified on Linux/macOS runs "bash -e {0}", bash runs "bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}", and sh runs "sh -e {0}". GitHub also accepts a custom template ("GitHub interprets the first whitespace-delimited word of the string as the command, and inserts the file name for the temporary script at {0}"). Line 119 lets any shell value that starts with bash or sh through, but line 127 then runs the fixed bash flags, so shell: bash -x {0} is run without -x. Variant ci-shell-bash-x-custom passes 26/26, while the same xtrace written as set -x in the script fails test 7 (ci-set-x). The grader therefore judges one xtrace form and not the other. Related model limits, all passing 26/26 and all deliberate shapes: only steps that reference a secret, or log in, are run, so cross-step channels are invisible. Examples are a login step writing the password to a file that a later step base64-prints (ci-cross-step-file), a later step that prints the Docker config file (ci-docker-config-cat), and a GITHUB_OUTPUT value echoed by a later step (ci-github-output). Reversed output (ci-reversed) is also missed, although the secrets page's own proofreader analogy names writing a phrase backwards.

-n1234". This rests on pflag's documented semantics, not on a page of Docker's docs, and was not run against a real docker binary. The form is uncommon, hence low; --username=VALUE (ci-username-equals-long) already passes.

evidence.section: Command line flag syntax: non-boolean and flags without a 'no option default value'

findings.recommendation: In optionValue, strip one leading "=" from an attached short-flag value (for example, "-u=" followed by the value yields the value).

findings.claim: Basis: a scratch copy of the frozen loop-5 export (HEAD c3e666bf; lab.json sha256 4968154e, tests/lab.mjs sha256 7403eb2f, tests/behavior.mjs sha256 1411ab6f, tests/service_behavior.py sha256 bfec51d8). npm run setup in tests (npm ci, then a venv with the 14 pins of tests/requirements.txt under Python 3.14.6; pip freeze equals the file and pip check is clean), Node v24.2.0, bash 3.2.57, macOS arm64. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's own solution, written from the README and topic pages, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. 158 one-change variants of that solution, plus a half-solved project, were each run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. They include every shape named in the loop-4 reconciliation's closed lists for ops-sme-003 (S1-S14), 008 (a1-a3 and the loop-2 lists), 010 (c1-c7, b1-b3), the guard list g1-g7/f1-f8 and the heredoc list H1-H9. The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. Windows support is claimed without any run and without a statement that it is unverified. lab.json lines 69-73 list windows, and README lines 44-46 give Windows commands, but the only execution evidence is macOS (coding-lab-solved-run.json: "Linux and Windows runs are not yet recorded"). This loop adds several Windows-only paths that nobody has run; the points below are reasoning, not runs. (1) findBash (behavior.mjs lines 55-64) resolves git --exec-path three levels up to bin\bash.exe. That is right for the standard Git for Windows layout and has a Program Files fallback. (2) The stand-in docker is an extensionless #!/bin/sh file. Whether MSYS bash's command -v finds and runs it relies on Git for Windows' noacl mount treating #! files as executable; if it does not, the line 155 guard reports that the stand-in could not be put first on PATH and tests 6-7 fail. (3) LAB_DOCKER_CALLS is passed to the POSIX stub as a Windows path. (4) shell: sh steps spawn "sh" from PATH (line 127), which a default Git for Windows install does not put on the Windows PATH. (5) labPython's .venv\Scripts\python.exe is the right venv layout, but py -3 may pick 3.10 (see ops-sme-r5-01). The LAB_BASH and LAB_PYTHON overrides that would let a learner work around (1) and (5) are not documented.
findings.recommendation: Either record a Windows run (setup plus starter and solved runs) as module evidence, or add one README line under Setup saying the Windows path has not yet been run, together with the LAB_BASH and LAB_PYTHON overrides. In runStep, resolve sh next to the found bash on Windows.

findings.claim: Basis: a scratch copy of the frozen loop-5 export (HEAD c3e666bf; lab.json sha256 4968154e, tests/lab.mjs sha256 7403eb2f, tests/behavior.mjs sha256 1411ab6f, tests/service_behavior.py sha256 bfec51d8). npm run setup in tests (npm ci, then a venv with the 14 pins of tests/requirements.txt under Python 3.14.6; pip freeze equals the file and pip check is clean), Node v24.2.0, bash 3.2.57, macOS arm64. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's own solution, written from the README and topic pages, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. 158 one-change variants of that solution, plus a half-solved project, were each run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. They include every shape named in the loop-4 reconciliation's closed lists for ops-sme-003 (S1-S14), 008 (a1-a3 and the loop-2 lists), 010 (c1-c7, b1-b3), the guard list g1-g7/f1-f8 and the heredoc list H1-H9. The half-solved project (S38 done, S39 untouched) gives 15/26, as README line 98 says. The Python pins are a coherent, installable set, but nothing verifies them. pip freeze in the created venv equals tests/requirements.txt exactly, pip check is clean, and a dry-run resolution with --only-binary=:all: finds wheels for all 14 pins on Python 3.11, 3.14 and 3.15 for Linux x86_64, macOS arm64 and win_amd64 (3.14 also on win_arm64). However, line 34 runs pip install -r without --require-hashes and without --only-binary=:all:. A compromised or replaced index file would therefore be installed, and on a platform without a wheel pip would silently build pydantic_core from source (which needs a Rust toolchain). Lab-contract section 5 asks for pinned versions with lockfiles, and the npm side is hash-locked through package-lock.json integrity. Also, setup honours LAB_PYTHON through labPython(), so a learner or tool that exports it makes npm run setup pip-install into that interpreter instead of the lab's .venv.
findings.recommendation: Add --hash=sha256:... entries to tests/requirements.txt (for example with pip-compile --generate-hashes) and pass --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: in setup_python.mjs. Make setup ignore LAB_PYTHON, which should be only a test-time override.
